data.why: The repo ships no example tiles, so three correctly-named overlapping tiles (sample_1.png, sample_2.png, sample_3.png, each a 48x16 bit pattern with ~40% horizontal overlap between neighbors) were synthesized so the app's upload, stitch, diagnostics and export steps can actually run.

goals: Upload a series of overlapping microscope tile images named <prefix>_N.<ext> and have the app sort and load them correctly
Stitch the tiles into a single calibrated panorama and confirm the result assembles without errors
Review the per-pair stitching diagnostics (method used, matches, inliers, translation, rotation) to judge stitch quality
Tune preprocessing and blending settings (CLAHE, feature detection thresholds, blending levels, gain compensation) and see how they change the panorama
Export the finished panorama image and the tile-positions CSV for downstream specimen-prep records

review.summary: The tree captures the stitcher's core workflow (load a numbered series, stitch, read per-pair diagnostics, tune, export the panorama and tile positions) with accurate labels, and 12 of the 13 screens checked support their nodes. Before filing, it needs capture planning moved up front as a real stage, a troubleshooting and sanity-check step, one variable per tuning task, a better screen for the CSV download, and Streamlit's generic widget actions and table toolbar demoted from tasks and features.
